title: Planning and deployment strategies of distributed energy systems for urban forms in the megacity: A case study of Beijing
abstract: This study proposes a priority-based decision framework for the city-scale deployment of distributed energy systems (DES), considering urban morphological and functional characteristics. Using K-means++ clustering, mixed-integer linear programming (MILP), and multi-criteria analysis, the framework integrates photovoltaic systems, energy storage, buildings, and the power grid. A case study of Beijing examines 21,104 urban units comprising more than 1.2 million buildings. The results demonstrate the potential of distributed energy systems to reduce peak electricity demand, renewable energy curtailment, and operational costs while identifying cost-effective deployment priorities across different urban forms.

title: Energy–Environment–Economy (3E) Analysis of the Performance of Introducing Photovoltaic and Energy Storage Systems into Residential Buildings: A Case Study in Shenzhen, China
abstract: This study evaluates the energy, environmental, and economic performance of photovoltaic (PV) and energy storage systems (ESSs) in residential buildings through a case study in Shenzhen, China. Four PV and storage strategies are compared using a comprehensive 3E assessment and sensitivity analysis. Results show that PV systems combined with batteries can reduce life-cycle carbon emissions by up to 44%, while PV systems integrated with ice storage offer favorable economic performance and potential carbon emission reductions of approximately 30%. The findings provide insights into low-carbon building energy system design and optimization.

title: Control-Oriented Prototype Energy Model for Data Centers
abstract: This study develops a high-fidelity, control-oriented prototype energy model for air-cooled data centers using co-simulation between Modelica and EnergyPlus. The proposed model incorporates detailed HVAC configurations, underfloor air distribution (UFAD), and dynamic IT equipment operation to represent realistic data center thermal behavior. A standardized co-simulation interface enables the integration, testing, and evaluation of advanced control strategies. Simulation results demonstrate physically consistent interactions between IT heat generation and HVAC thermal responses, providing a reproducible framework for data center energy performance analysis and control development.
citation: H. Li, S. Huang, and W. Zuo, "Control-Oriented Prototype Energy Model for Data Centers," Proceedings of SimBuild 2026, pp. 287–295, 2026. doi:10.26868/30680611.2026.1310.
